ABSTRACT: Chiral allenyl phosphine oxides represent a significant kind of synthetic target with promising potential for various
applications. However, explorations toward their asymmetric synthesis remain scarce, primarily due to the competitive coordination
of phosphine oxides with metal catalysts. Herein, we report a Pd-catalyzed enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine
oxide for the eficient construction of a variety of chiral allenyl phosphine oxides. The success of this reaction arises from the
enhanced (bidentate form) coordination of a newly designed, fungicide-inspired enyne-type propargylic carbamate with a chiral Pd
complex. This protocol features high yields and enantioselectivities, scalability, and versatile derivatization. Mechanistic studies
confirmed the exclusion of a kinetic resolution pathway.

■ INTRODUCTION
Chiral allenes are privileged motifs in natural products,
bioactive molecules, and functional materials.<sup>1</sup> Consequently,
recent decades have witnessed significant advances in the
development of catalytic methods toward their asymmetric
synthesis.<sup>2</sup> As a result, a wide variety of chiral allenes bearing
diverse functional groups could be obtained conveniently
through asymmetric catalysis approaches.<sup>3</sup> On the other hand,
phosphine oxides that are incorporated within various chiral
scafolds are widely used as organocatalysts and ligands for
metal catalysis (Figure 1a). Related synthesis has attracted
more and more attention.<sup>4,5</sup> Despite elegant progresses that
have been made in both areas, a method to access chiral allenyl
phosphine oxides remains unexplored until very recently, Ma,
Zhang, Qian, and Zhang jointly published the first Pd-
catalyzed enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine
oxides (SPOs) (during which we are also preparing this
manuscript).<sup>6</sup> Previously, Ma, Zhang, and Qian pioneered the
asymmetric allenylation of H-phosphonates (2022), represent-
ing the sole, highly valuable example of a catalytic approach to
axially chiral allenyl phosphonates.<sup>7</sup> This breakthrough
suggested that SPOs might also serve as viable substrates for
the concise construction of chiral allenyl phosphine oxides via
transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric allenylation reaction.
However, SPOs undergo facile tautomerization to trivalent
R<sup>1</sup>R<sup>2</sup>P−OH species more readily than H-phosphonates,
leading to competitive metal coordination that suppresses
the desired allenylation pathway (Figure 1b).<sup>8</sup> To address this,
several elegant strategies were developed to avoid the
involvement of trivalent R<sup>1</sup>R<sup>2</sup>P−OH species. Guo presented
a Ni-catalyzed O-propargylation/Horner-Mark cascade to
construct chiral allenyl phosphine oxides directly.<sup>9</sup> Meanwhile,
Zhang developed a Ni-catalyzed asymmetric S 2′ functional-
ization of phosphines, with subsequent oxidation delivering
chiral allenyl phosphine oxides.<sup>10</sup> He reported an asymmetric
synergistic Pd/Co-catalyzed hydrophosphinylation of enynes
using a newly designed masked phosphinylating reagent,
enabling eficient access to novel allenylic phosphine oxides
with P-stereocenter.<sup>11</sup> Despite these advances, methods for
direct allenyl C(sp<sup>2</sup>)−P bond construction remain highly
sought-after yet scarce, presenting a persistent synthetic
challenge.

application of novel fungicide-inspired π−allyl Pd precursors
particularly for the construction of tetrasubstituted axially
chiral allenes,

lective allenylation of SPOs. This transformation utilizes a
newly designed, Vinclozolin-inspired enyne-type propargylic
carbamate, providing new access to a class of highly
functionalized, tetrasubstituted chiral allenes bearing allenyl
amide, phosphine oxide, and alkene moieties (Figure 1e). This

catalyzed systems in two key aspects: (i) The strategic
incorporation of a terminal alkene group enables eficient
generation of novel, reactive chiral vinylidene-π-allyl palladium
intermediates for asymmetric construction of chiral allenes and
(ii) the implementation of Vinclozolin-inspired enyne-type
propargylic carbamates, featuring quaternary chiral centers,
enabled direct construction of tetrasubstituted chiral allenes
having phosphonyl unit.

With optimized conditions established, a range of function-
alized substrates 2 were evaluated (Scheme 1). Initial
investigation of nitrogen substituents (R<sup>1</sup>) revealed that
substrates bearing either electron-donating (Me, OMe) or
electron-withdrawing groups (F, Cl, Br, CN, and COOMe) at
the meta- or para-position aforded the corresponding products
in moderate to high yields (3aa−3ai, 29−90%) with
consistently high enantioselectivity (90−93% ee). It was
observed that para-substituted electron-deficient substrates
tended to exhibit lower reaction eficiency, suggesting that the
electronic properties of the amide moiety play a key role in the
transformation. As illustrated in the proposed mechanism, this
may be attributed to the amide functioning as a base to
facilitate deprotonation of the SPO substrate. Sterically
demanding substrates, ortho-chlorophenyl (2j) and 1-naph-
thyl-substituted substrate (2m), produced product 3aj (22%
yield, 88% ee) and 3am (55% yield, 64% ee) in significantly
reduced yield or ee, respectively. These results indicated that
steric hindrance in the substrate exerted a pronounced negative
efect on the eficiency and stereocontrol of the reaction. 3,4-
Dimethylphenyl substrate 2k performed well to provide
product 3ak in 83% yield with 92% ee, contrasting sharply
with the performance of its dichlorophenyl analogue 2l (its
product, 3al, 26% yield, 58% ee). Notably, N-alkyl-substituted
variants such as N-ethyl (2n) and N-benzyl (2o) substrates
proved to be unreactive. Variations of Ar groups were also
investigated. Similar to the situation of R<sup>1</sup>, para-substituted
aromatics bearing electron-donating groups presented higher
reactivity (3ap, 3aq), compared with that of the electron-
withdrawing group (3ar). meta-Methylphenyl and meta-
fluorophenyl substrates were also compatible with the reaction
to deliver the corresponding products 3as and 3at in both
moderate yield and high ee. However, the ortho-tolyl-
substituted substrate 2u exhibited good reactivity but
compromised enantioselectivity, likely due to steric constraints
imposed by the ortho-methyl group.
